record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Let µ(t) be a continuous monotonic increasing function of t for t ∈ [0, 1] and let ω1 (h, µ), ω2 (h, µ) denote its modulus of continuity and modulus of smoothness respectively. It is known that, if ω1 (h) = O(h) (h → 0), or ω2 (h) = O(h(log 1/h)−c ) (h → 0), where c > 12 , then µ(t) is absolutely continuous (w.r.t. Lebesgue measure). It is also known that each of these conditions is essentially best-possible. Are they simultane- ously best possible? More precisely, is it true that given any function φ(t) ↑ ∞ as t ↓ 0, there is a continuous, monotonic increasing singular function µ(t) such that ω1 (h) = O(hφ(h)) (h → 0) and ω2 (h) = O(h(log 1/h)− 2 ) (h → 0)? (J. M. Anderson)

artifact.category_tag: modulus of continuity and singular functions
artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a continuous function $\mu:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$, define its modulus of continuity by
$$\omega_1(h,\mu) = \sup\{|\mu(t+s)-\mu(t)| : t,t+s\in[0,1],\ 0\le s\le h\},$$
and its modulus of smoothness by
$$\omega_2(h,\mu) = \sup\{|\mu(t+s)+\mu(t-s)-2\mu(t)| : t-s,t+s\in[0,1],\ 0\le s\le h\}.$$
It is known that if $\mu$ is continuous and monotonic increasing on $[0,1]$ and either
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\omega_1(h,\mu)=O(h)$ as $h\to 0^+$, or
\item[(b)] $\omega_2(h,\mu)=O\!\left(h(\log 1/h)^{-c}\right)$ as $h\to 0^+$ for some $c>\tfrac12$,
\end{enumerate}
then $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$. Each of these conditions is individually known to be essentially best possible.

Question: Are these two conditions simultaneously essentially best possible? Specifically, prove or disprove the following statement: for every function $\varphi:(0,1]\to(0,\infty)$ with $\varphi(t)\to\infty$ as $t\to 0^+$, there exists a continuous, monotonic increasing singular function $\mu:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ (i.e., $\mu'=0$ almost everywhere with respect to Lebesgue measure, but $\mu$ is non-constant) such that
$$\omega_1(h,\mu) = O(h\,\varphi(h)) \quad\text{and}\quad \omega_2(h,\mu) = O\!\left(h(\log 1/h)^{-1/2}\right) \quad\text{as } h\to 0^+.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been resolved affirmatively: Anderson, Fernández and Shields constructed continuous monotonic increasing singular functions with the prescribed simultaneous moduli, showing the two conditions are simultaneously best possible.
